title: Place of Worship Emoji 🛐 Meaning: Prayer and Stan Praise
description: 🛐 is a neutral symbol for prayer and worship, and in fan slang it means "I worship this." See both meanings of the place of worship emoji and when each fits.
summary: The 🛐 place of worship emoji shows a figure kneeling in prayer on a purple tile. It is a faith-neutral symbol for prayer, worship, or a prayer room. Online, it is just as often used as playful slang for adoring someone or something, as in "I worship her 🛐."
meaning: Unlike ⛪, 🕌, or 🕍, this emoji does not name a religion. It was added in 2015 alongside other religious symbols as a general sign for worship, and its kneeling figure fits many traditions. Religious users send it for going to pray, for a time of devotion, or to ask others to join in prayer, and multifaith groups find it useful precisely because it belongs to no single community.

The slang meaning took off in fan culture. On stan Twitter, TikTok, and Instagram comments, 🛐 means "I worship this," a dramatic bow to a celebrity, a song, a fictional character, or even a perfect sandwich. Strings like 🛐🛐🛐 under a new album announcement are pure hype, and "mother 🛐" or "queen 🛐" are common under photos of admired performers.

Because both meanings are live, context decides. From a parish group or a friend asking for prayers, it is sincere. Under a pop star's selfie, it is exaggerated praise with no religious content. Some believers find the casual "worship" usage irreverent, while others shrug at it as obvious hyperbole, in the same way people say they "worship" a favorite band.

A third, practical use is wayfinding. The kneeling figure resembles the icons used for prayer rooms and chapels in airports, hospitals, and universities, so people sometimes use 🛐 when pointing out where to pray in a building or on a trip. Chaplaincies and campus ministries also use it in posters and posts about quiet rooms open to students and staff of every faith.

contexts.label: On stan Twitter and TikTok
contexts.body: Fans flood replies with 🛐 when an idol posts, drops music, or does something iconic. It is the emoji equivalent of falling to your knees. It also praises food, outfits, and art: "this lasagna 🛐." No religious statement is intended, and the tone is hyperbolic and fun.

contexts.label: In prayer requests
contexts.body: Religious users of many faiths send 🛐 to say they are going to pray, to ask for prayer, or to mark a time of devotion such as adoration, salah, or a vigil. Because it is generic, it suits interfaith settings and messages to groups whose members practice different religions.

contexts.label: When traveling
contexts.body: The kneeling figure echoes the prayer room symbol found in many airports and hospitals. Travelers use 🛐 to share where a chapel or quiet room is, or to note that they found a place to pray between flights. In this use it is purely informational.

examples.text: She just dropped the tour dates 🛐🛐🛐
examples.meaning: Fan excitement and adoration for a performer, not literal worship.

examples.text: Holy hour at 7 tonight in the chapel 🛐
examples.meaning: An invitation to Eucharistic adoration or prayer at a set time.

examples.text: Found the prayer room at gate B12 🛐
examples.meaning: Practical travel info about where to pray in an airport.
The food is so good it deserves worship; affectionate exaggeration.

examples.text: Please keep our family in your prayers this week 🛐
examples.meaning: A sincere request for prayer from people of any faith.

combos.meaning: Overwhelmed admiration, as if moved to tears by greatness.
Earnest prayer, or extra-strong reverence for something.
Bowing to royalty: praise for someone called a queen or king.
Quiet prayer or a vigil, often in memory of someone.

confusedWith.difference: ⛪ is a Christian church building with a cross, used for Mass, services, and weddings. 🛐 is a generic symbol for worship that points to no specific religion or building.
🧎 is an ordinary person kneeling, which can mean proposing, resting, or begging. 🛐 shows a kneeling figure as a worship symbol on a tile, so it reads as prayer or reverence.
🙇 bows deeply in apology or gratitude, a gesture rooted in Japanese etiquette. 🛐 is about worship, either religious or as fan slang.

avoid: Do not use the joking "worship" sense in replies to someone's sincere prayer request or religious post.
Avoid assuming a 🛐 from a fan account is religious; it is almost always hyperbolic praise.
design: A small white figure kneeling and bowing forward with hands raised or joined, on a purple square like the other religion symbols. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft all follow this pictogram style. The figure has no clothing or features that would tie it to a particular faith, which is the point of the design.

faqs.a: Usually "I worship this." Fans post it under creators, celebrities, and anything they find amazing. It is exaggerated praise and has nothing to do with religion in that setting.
None in particular. It is a neutral symbol for worship and prayer, designed to apply to any faith. For specific traditions, emojis such as ⛪, 🕌, 🕍, and 🛕 exist.

faqs.q: Is it disrespectful to use 🛐 for celebrities?
faqs.a: Most people read it as harmless exaggeration. Some religious users find it irreverent, especially in large amounts. Keeping fan-praise usage away from genuine prayer conversations avoids any clash.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🛐 and 🙏?
faqs.a: 🙏 means thanks, please, or prayer and is used far more widely. 🛐 is specifically worship: a full bow before something sacred, or in slang, before someone you idolize.
